title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Fleet Ledger. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Fleet Ledger
options.lineage: ship's logs, technical reference manuals, ruled ledger books
options.thesis: The fleet as a bound ledger — every model a ruled entry, every question a tabbed section you consult, not a dashboard you watch.
options.viewport: A tabbed ledger open at the fleet index: the five questions as tabs down the fore edge, models as ruled entries with mono IDs and measured figures.
options.risk: Reads nostalgic when the type is set timidly.

raised.raise: The ledger's five question-tabs are a stepped rail down the fore edge, height proportional to each section's extent.
Each model entry carries a monumental mono ID and a status mark that reads at a glance, like a gate number.

options.label: The Instrument Panel
options.thesis: The fleet as a cockpit — every model a live instrument, every question a gauge.
options.viewport: A console of gauges: the five questions as instrument clusters, models as readouts with status lamps.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Data-Sublime Field
options.thesis: The fleet as a dense barcode field — pure black and white, mono numerics, hairline bars.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline bars with dense mono numbers; the fleet as a frozen barcode.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — the fleet IS dense data; loses narrowly on clarity for an occasional reference.
options.risk: The strobing/inversion is hostile to a reference artifact.

options.label: Celestial Star Atlas
options.thesis: The fleet as a sky — models as magnitude-scaled stars on a navy chart.
options.viewport: A coordinate sphere of models, dot diameter carrying size, constellation lines faint beneath.
options.case: Resonant — a fleet as a sky of models; the star metaphor can obscure tabular data.
options.risk: Models aren't stars; the metaphor may fight the data.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: The fleet as a concourse — saturated yellow bands, monumental gate numbers, decision points.
options.viewport: Framed yellow bands hanging over the fleet, each model a gate with a monumental number.
options.case: Strong — a fleet catalog IS wayfinding through dense information; gates map to models cleanly.
options.risk: Yellow at full saturation across a reference artifact is loud.

options.label: Acetate Reference Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals, acetate tab boards
options.thesis: The fleet as an open manual — milk acetate leaves over a section-hue board, a stepped tab rail down the fore edge.
options.viewport: A manual open at a tabbed section; the five questions as a stepped tab rail, models as ruled leaves.
options.case: The strongest fit — a reference manual is exactly what this is; the tab rail maps to the five questions.
options.risk: The acetate/leaf metaphor needs disciplined execution to not read as gimmick.

options.label: Monochrome Product Surface
options.thesis: The fleet in one neutral scale with a single restrained accent, claim-and-proof pairs.
options.viewport: Near-black on near-white, one accent used sparingly, each claim paired with a proof.
options.case: A marketing grammar, not a reference tool; claim-and-proof pairs don't fit a data catalog.
options.risk: Reads as a landing page, not a reference artifact.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: The fleet as a cast of rounded mascots ranked by popularity across a pastel grid.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of mascots, each with a name plate and a one-line personality note.
options.case: Wrong register — a playful consumer catalog, not an ops instrument; mascots for models is a category mismatch.

canonCard.label: Standard Data Dashboard
canonCard.thesis: The fleet as a conventional dark dashboard — cards, badges, sortable table.
canonCard.viewport: A stats strip, filter chips, and a sortable table of models.
canonCard.risk: The generic AI look you're trying to escape.
